title: Converting data to JSON and handling model responses
summary: Shape retrieved rows into JSON for the model, send them, and extract the response safely.

items: Convert structured data to JSON for language-model processing.
Send results to a model and extract its response.
Evaluate correctness and prevent unsafe generated SQL.

blocks.body: The last mile of RAG is data shaping and response handling — plus the safety concerns of AI-generated SQL, an explicit production concern in DP-800.

terms.definition: The retrieved data supplied to the model to answer from.
Translating natural language into SQL, which must be validated before execution.

blocks.body: Use **`FOR JSON`** / JSON constructors to convert rows to the JSON the model expects, **send** via the REST endpoint, and **extract** the answer with `JSON_VALUE`/`OPENJSON`. For natural-language-to-SQL, treat generated SQL as untrusted: validate against an allow-list, run read-only with least privilege, and block destructive statements.

blocks.heading: Safe natural-language-to-SQL
blocks.body: An agent turns a question into SQL. Before executing, parse and reject anything that isn't a single SELECT, run it as a low-privilege read-only principal (reinforced by RLS), enforce a row/time limit, and log the query. This prevents unsafe or destructive generated SQL.

items.fix: Validate, constrain to read-only least-privilege, and block DDL/DML before running.

blocks.body: Run AI-generated queries under a least-privilege, read-only identity with RLS; validate for correctness and safety; never allow destructive statements.

tips: FOR JSON shapes the payload; JSON_VALUE extracts the answer.
Generated SQL must be validated and sandboxed (read-only, least privilege).

blocks.body: Convert rows with FOR JSON, call the model, extract with JSON_VALUE, and rigorously sandbox any AI-generated SQL to read-only least privilege.
